steps.narration: The row of three runs out while two objects remain in the row of five. Three is the smaller group.

widget.prompt: There are 7 hearts. Build a star group with FEWER stars.

commonCounts.feedback: Seven stars pair off evenly with seven hearts; that is SAME, not fewer.
Eight stars leave a star standing alone; that is MORE, not fewer.

widget.missFeedback: Build fewer stars than seven — any count that runs out first.
widget.successFeedback: Five stars run out with two hearts still waiting — fewer, exactly as asked.

predict.prompt: Fewer stars than hearts — which side runs out first while pairing?
predict.reveal: Fewer means the group that empties first, leaving the other side holding extras.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm smaller group.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm smaller group uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: There are 8 stars and 10 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Equal needs the pairing to come out even; here one side is left holding extras (8 against 10).

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Correct — 10 hearts against 8 stars; pairing one to one leaves hearts unmatched.

options.label: More stars
options.feedback: Pairing one to one uses every star with hearts to spare, so the stars are not the larger group.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and look at which side has leftovers.

widget.prompt: What number comes right before 9? Hop one back and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 9 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop back to reach 8.
7 goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 1 hop back from 9 to reach 8.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 back from 9: you land on 8.
widget.successFeedback: 8 — one hop back, and one hop earlier in the song always means less.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — one hop back from 9 reaches 8.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right before 9 means a single hop back, stopping on 8.

widget.prompt: Why does pairing one to one tell you which group is smaller?

options.label: The side that runs out of matches first is the smaller group
options.feedback: Correct — pairing empties the smaller side first, before the bigger side runs out of partners.

options.label: The smaller group is the one written second
options.feedback: Order on the page never decides size — pairing settles it, not writing order.

options.label: The smaller group takes up less table space
options.feedback: Table space can trick you — a spread-out small group can look big without adding members.

options.label: The smaller group has smaller objects
options.feedback: Pairing counts members, not the size of each object — a big object still pairs with a small one.
